name: rules-ontology
what: Sign-ins, the Ontology view with the sign-in file (auth) opened: its three rules set on columns, each in words with what a broken row does (Method one of its five values, else the day holds; Latency 0 to 30,000 ms and Country never blank, else the row is flagged), each with Change and Remove for the owner, and an Add a rule button on every column's card; a note that the file's meanings and rules are shared (examples/ontologies/auth.json), with its download

text: Method is Password, Single sign-on, MFA push, Passkey or API key, and nothing the ontology doesn’t have: else hold the day
Latency is from 0 to 30,000 ms: else flag the row and keep it
Country is never blank: else flag the row and keep it
Shared. auth’s meanings and rules come from ../ontologies/auth.json, which every flow that reads auth imports
noText: Not checked: switched off in auth_valid’s cell

name: rules-add-form
what: The owner taps Add a check on the User card, and has edits take effect from the day on screen (Thu Mar 21, ADR 0021 §5; they reach every day recorded after it, to Mon Mar 25, too): the form in place of the button, what User must be (never blank by default), what a row that breaks it does, Add the check and Cancel

pageText: For auth only. On once saved
Back-dated: 5 recorded days (Thu Mar 21 to Mon Mar 25, 1 published) run again under the new rules, and one decision restates them.

name: rules-why
what: Saving a rule asks why (ADR 0027 §2, Q-256): the kind of change, one of four with the one the edit usually is picked, and a reason, both required; who decided, what led to it and the thinking fold away beneath. Without a reason it says one is needed

.vf-detail: A change needs a reason: one line of why.
Who decided, what led to it, the thinking

name: rules-added
what: The rule added, in force from Thu Mar 21: the five days recorded from Thu 21 run again under it and come out the same (Fri 22 still held for its renamed column, the three days after it at the gate), and the restatement opens for its sign-off (Q-199 as answered, ADR 0022 §1); User is never blank, else flag the row and keep it, listed on the User card and among the changes above the files; the check cell auth_valid gains user_required: 'on' in its ontology list
clicks: A sign-in without its user can’t be traced

pageText: User is never blank: else flag the row and keep it
Added a rule to auth: User is never blank, else flag the row and keep it, in force from Thu Mar 21
The new rules change no published day
Sign off 5 days as the same

name: rules-signed-off
what: The restatement opened from the day's head, and the two days that came out the same signed off with a reason: one restatement recorded, nothing decided again
clicks: The same day under the new rule: User is never blank

expect.status: ^5 recorded days ran again under the new rules: they come out the same\. Signed off and recorded\.$

name: rules-tab
what: The sign-in file's import card, Rules tab: its four rules, each with a switch (on), what a broken row does, and what the run on screen counted

text: Method is Password, Single sign-on, MFA push, Passkey or API key

name: rules-switched-off
what: Latency's rule switched off on the import card: struck through, Off, not enforced, written into the check cell auth_valid (its ontology list), recorded as a flow change

text: Switched off a rule of auth: Latency is from 0 to 30,000 ms, in auth_valid (from Thu Mar 21)
Sign off 5 days as the same

name: rules-switch-signed-off
what: Signed off too, from the day's head, with its reason
clicks: Latency is checked elsewhere: the day the same

expect.status: ^5 recorded days ran again under the new rules: they come out the same\. Signed off and recorded\.$

name: rules-cell-written
what: The import card's Rules tab after both: three of four on, Latency's struck through, and the check cell as written, latency_ms_range: 'off' and user_required: 'on' in its ontology list

name: rules-reload
what: After a reload, Thu Mar 21's third version: each edit ran the day again and came out the same, so the day opens on the version readers had (Q-199 amended), and its third is the day run again under both edits: the rules as edited, in force on it, four, Latency's off

name: rules-ontology-off
what: The Ontology view says Latency's rule is switched off in auth_valid's cell

text: Not checked: switched off in auth_valid’s cell

name: rules-tab-dark
what: The Rules tab in dark, in a fresh browser: the three rules the flow ships with
